title: Boss Level 2: The Number Guessing Game
concepts: randrange() stops before its end value
checking input with strip() and isdigit() before int()
while loop with a try counter and break
testing a random program with a fixed secret

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for a number from 1 to 20 including both ends, the AI wrote random.randrange(1, 20) and said every number from 1 to 20 could be picked. randrange stops before its end value, like range(), so 20 is never picked: 10,000 draws gave a highest number of 19. randint(1, 20) includes 20.

changes: As the curriculum's change note says, this project introduces import and the random module minimally (randint, randrange and seed); modules are covered fully in Chapter 18.
Input is checked with strip() from Chapter 3 and the string method isdigit(), which is new here, because try and except arrive in Chapter 22.

The finished game project/guessing_game.py picks a truly random secret, so it has no fixed expected output and is listed in support_files. Every test is a copy (examples/test_*.py) with one changed line, a fixed secret, and its own typed answers, and these copies are verified.
An answer that is not a whole number from 1 to 20 does not count as a try, so a typing mistake never costs the player a guess.
outstanding_issues: The traceback for the word crash shows the short file name; on a learner's computer the full path appears instead.
The seeded examples gave the same numbers on Python 3.13 to 3.15; a future Python version could change them, and the verifier would then report it.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
